question: How does the military complex look, whole and destroyed? Alex's second mission profile (decision suppress-mission): 'Clear mobile Aa units and their escorts to enable a bombing run of a military complex.'
source: scripts/ui/boards/military_complex_board_shot.gd: the new generator in scripts/ui/unit_marker_art_static.gd (the military complex section), drawn through the game's own markers (scripts/ui/unit_marker.gd) and baked art by scripts/ui/boards/m2_frame.gd, on the game's own paper and road; the ruin is the art UnitMarkerArtStatic.complex_ruin_art bakes, placed as the effects layer would place a ruin. No sandbox is stood up and nothing in the game changes but the art cache

held_constant.scale: the MAP's (2 px per metre x zoom: 2 at zoom 1, 4 at zoom 2, about 0.8 at the planning zoom 0.35, a little over the map's 0.7 because the planes' 14 px floor holds the marker rule), data military_complex.map_scale_factor 0.5 of the marker rule (PROPOSED); the tower and the battery beside it at the game's rule for static units (twice the planes')
held_constant.footprint: 80 x 60 m with the fence 4 m inside it (data military_complex.footprint_m, PROPOSED)
held_constant.light: the map's sun (north-west, elevation 46, shadow strength 0.44), every part cast by its height (data heights_m)
held_constant.pen: the game's own pen (render_defaults linework.pen, shadow side)
held_constant.accent: one zone per look: a recognition panel on the main roof, on the lit half, in the enemy's slate blue (side_b)
held_constant.destroyed: R1's language (the tower's ruin: scorch, pale-lipped craters, the hall roofless with a torn roof lying across it, heaps, the fence half down), no fire; the smoke column is the effects layer's
held_constant.data_that_changes_between_options: ui.json unit_art.variant.military_complex (the look index) and nothing else

parameter: data/ui/unit_art_mission2.json military_complex.default_look (PROPOSED: 0, the hangar yard) until Alex picks; ui.json unit_art.variant.military_complex overrides it once the pick is made

options.name: A
options.title: Hangar yard
options.description: A big barrel-roofed hangar on a pale concrete apron in the north of the fence, two sheds and two round fuel tanks, trucks in the packed-earth yard, a gatehouse on the south fence, and watch towers at two corners. The accent is a recognition panel on the hangar roof.

options.name: B
options.title: Works with a saw-tooth hall
options.description: A long factory hall with a saw-tooth roof (a shaded strip and a lit strip, repeated), a tall chimney whose long shadow is the tell at the planning zoom, a boiler house, a coal heap and three long sheds, inside a wire fence with a gate on the west. The accent is a recognition panel on the hall's roof.

options.name: C
options.title: Barracks and depot
options.description: Three long barracks ranges round a three-sided yard, a depot shed closing the fourth side, with a flagpole, parked vehicles and stacked crates, inside a low wall (the village's compound wall) with a gatehouse on the south. The accent is a recognition panel on the middle range's roof.

palette_check: No option adds a hue and the only accent is the one roof panel (side_b L 0.551 C 0.100). Surfaces are the paper ramp the village uses (roof lit L 0.922, roof shaded L 0.752, wall fill L 0.880, object fill L 0.925 against paper L 0.847); the ruin uses R1's roles (char = dirt at 0.55 L 0.632 over paper, pit = ink at 0.17). Material is linework.
recommendation_proposed: A, the hangar yard, as the working default (PROPOSED by Track M2U, Alex decides): the clearest silhouette at the planning zoom (one long pale roof, a pale apron, round tanks) and the most obviously a target for a bomber; its blue panel sits on the lit half of a big pale roof where it reads best. B is the most distinctive at distance (the saw-tooth block and the chimney's long shadow, the same kind of tell as the tower's lattice) at the price of the most drawing; C is the quietest and the most like the village.
wiring_note: The standing complex is wired through unit_marker_art.gd's one dispatch line (silhouette military_complex). The DESTROYED look is baked by UnitMarkerArtStatic.complex_ruin_art(style, ppm, rot) and is NOT wired: a destroyed static unit's marker goes at its down_at and the effects layer's ruin (scripts/fx, fx.ruin(unit, pos, t, kind, size, heading)) takes its place, so the effects layer needs a kind 'military_complex' that blits this art in place of its battery scorch.
sheet: board.png (each look whole and destroyed at zoom 1, the planning zoom 1:1 and 3x, zoom 2, and turned; a palette strip)
chosen: A, the hangar yard (Alex 2026-10-11: 'And the hanger yard')
